title: Triangle Trigonometry and Vectors
description: A ramp rises 0.84 meter over a horizontal run of 7.2 meters. Find its angle of inclination and length.
outcomes: Connect unit-circle trig definitions with ratios in similar right triangles.
Model heights, distances, slopes, and angles of elevation or depression.
Derive and apply the Law of Sines to ASA, AAS, and suitable SSA triangles.
Determine whether SSA data produce zero, one, or two triangles.
Use the Law of Cosines for SAS and SSS data and connect it to the Pythagorean theorem.
Use K=(1/2)ab sin C and compare with base-height and Heron forms.
Translate among standard angles, quadrant bearings, headings, and triangle or component models.
Represent vectors by magnitude and direction, add them geometrically, and convert to components.
Use scalar multiplication, normalization, and component resolution.
Use the dot product to find angles, test orthogonality, and calculate projections.
